```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Source and model

```{r models, include = FALSE}
mod_er <- readModelDb("Ueno_2018_daclatasvir_asunaprevir_svr12")
mod_dcv <- readModelDb("Osawa_2018_daclatasvir")
mod_asv <- readModelDb("Osawa_2018_asunaprevir")
meta_er <- rxode2::rxode2(mod_er)$meta
```

* Citation: `r meta_er$reference`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.1262>
* PubMed Central: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6175176/>
* Supporting Information (Supplementary Tables 1-4 and Figure 1): distributed
  with the open-access article.

Ueno 2018 relates the probability of sustained virologic response 12 weeks
after the end of treatment (SVR12) to the average steady-state plasma
concentrations (Cav,ss) of daclatasvir (DCV) and asunaprevir (ASV) in Japanese
patients with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotype 1b infection treated with
the all-oral DUAL regimen for 24 weeks. The model is a binary logistic
regression fitted in NONMEM 7.2. The final logit is linear and uncentred in both
exposures, has a product (interaction) term, has **no intercept**, and adds a
shift for the baseline NS5A Y93H resistance-associated variant and another for
a missing Y93H result:

$$
\mathrm{logit}\,P(\mathrm{SVR12}) = \beta_1 C_{av,ss,\mathrm{ASV}} +
\beta_2 C_{av,ss,\mathrm{DCV}} + \beta_3 C_{av,ss,\mathrm{ASV}}
C_{av,ss,\mathrm{DCV}} + \mathrm{CAT}_1 \cdot \mathrm{Y93H} +
\mathrm{CAT}_2 \cdot \mathrm{Y93H}_{\mathrm{missing}}
$$

The exposures were not measured. Ueno 2018 predicted them from the companion
population PK models of the same two studies, which this package carries as
`Osawa_2018_daclatasvir` and `Osawa_2018_asunaprevir`. The exposure-response
model therefore takes the two Cav,ss values as data columns
(`CAV_DACLATASVIR`, `CAV_ASUNAPREVIR`, ng/mL). The last part of this article
regenerates those columns from the PK models.

# Population

```{r population, echo = FALSE}
pop <- meta_er$population
tibble::tibble(
  Field = c("Subjects", "Studies", "Age", "Weight", "Female", "Disease", "Dosing", "Region"),
  Value = c(
    pop$n_subjects, pop$n_studies, pop$age_range, pop$weight_range,
    paste0(pop$sex_female_pct, "%"), pop$disease_state, pop$dose_range, pop$regions
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Analysis population (Ueno 2018 Table 1 and Methods).")
```

All 265 patients were Japanese and had genotype 1b infection. 222 came from the
phase 3 study AI447026 (DCV 60 mg tablet once daily with ASV 100 mg softgel
capsule twice daily) and 43 from the phase 2 study AI447017 (DCV 60 mg once
daily with ASV 600 mg or 200 mg tablet twice daily). The NS5A Y93H variant was
present at baseline in 40 patients (15.1%) and unknown in 8 (3.0%). Observed
SVR12 was 90.3% without and 47.5% with baseline Y93H.

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Logistic link, no intercept | `logit P = b1 ASV + b2 DCV + b3 ASV DCV + ...` | Methods, logit equations; Results, Model Development ('without intercept, had the lowest BIC') |
| `e_cav_asunaprevir_logit` | 0.0069 per ng/mL | Table 2, 'Slope of ASV (b1)' |
| `e_cav_daclatasvir_logit` | 0.00368 per ng/mL | Table 2, 'Slope of DCV (b2)' |
| `e_cav_asunaprevir_daclatasvir_logit` | -9.12e-6 per (ng/mL)^2 | Table 2, 'Interaction between ASV and DCV (b3) (b x 10^-3)', printed -0.00912 |
| `e_hcv_ns5a_y93h_logit` | -2.53 | Table 2, 'Y93H (CAT1)' |
| `e_hcv_ns5a_y93h_missing_logit` | -0.508 | Table 2, 'Y93H Missing (CAT2)' |
| `addSd_prob_svr12` | 0.001, fixed | Not from the source (placeholder; see Assumptions) |
| Exposure columns | Cav,ss in ng/mL | Methods; Table 1 (medians and ranges) |

# Checks against the paper's printed numbers

## The interaction coefficient carries a factor of 10^-3

Table 2 prints the interaction row as '-0.00912' in a row headed
'(b x 10^-3)'. The Discussion prints four model-based SVR12 rates at the
analysis-set median exposures. They decide the reading: only the scaled value
reproduces them.

```{r scaling}
cav_dcv_med <- 557.4 # Table 1, DCV 60 mg once daily
cav_asv_med <- c(softgel_100 = 163.7, tablet_200 = 268.4) # Table 1

typical_logit <- function(asv, dcv, b3) {
  0.0069 * asv + 0.00368 * dcv + b3 * asv * dcv
}
data.frame(
  reading = c("b3 = -0.00912e-3", "b3 = -0.00912 (as printed)"),
  p_svr12_softgel = plogis(c(
    typical_logit(cav_asv_med[["softgel_100"]], cav_dcv_med, -0.00912e-3),
    typical_logit(cav_asv_med[["softgel_100"]], cav_dcv_med, -0.00912)
  ))
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4, caption = "SVR12 probability without Y93H at the softgel-regimen medians under the two readings of the interaction row. The paper reports 91.2%.")
```

## Model-based SVR12 rates (Discussion)

The packaged model is solved at the four exposure / Y93H combinations the
Discussion quotes. The probabilities are deterministic, so the check is tight.

```{r discussion-rates}
# The logistic model has no between-subject variability, so rxode2 warns that
# a multi-subject solve has no omega. That is expected; only that warning is
# muffled.
muffle_no_omega <- function(expr) {
  withCallingHandlers(expr, warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  })
}

solve_er <- function(asv, dcv, y93h, y93h_missing = 0) {
  ev <- data.frame(
    id = seq_along(asv),
    time = 0,
    amt = 0,
    evid = 0L,
    CAV_ASUNAPREVIR = asv,
    CAV_DACLATASVIR = dcv,
    HCV_NS5A_Y93H = y93h,
    HCV_NS5A_Y93H_MISSING = y93h_missing
  )
  muffle_no_omega(as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod_er,
    events = ev,
    returnType = "data.frame"
  )))$prob_svr12
}

disc <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~asv, ~y93h, ~published_pct,
  "ASV 100 mg BID softgel", 163.7, 0, 91.2,
  "ASV 100 mg BID softgel", 163.7, 1, 45.5,
  "ASV 200 mg BID tablet", 268.4, 0, 92.7,
  "ASV 200 mg BID tablet", 268.4, 1, 50.2
) |>
  mutate(
    dcv = cav_dcv_med,
    model_pct = 100 * solve_er(asv, dcv, y93h),
    diff_pts = model_pct - published_pct
  )

disc |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "ASV regimen" = regimen,
    "ASV Cav,ss (ng/mL)" = asv,
    "DCV Cav,ss (ng/mL)" = dcv,
    "Y93H" = y93h,
    "Published SVR12 (%)" = published_pct,
    "Model SVR12 (%)" = model_pct,
    "Difference (points)" = diff_pts
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Model-based SVR12 at the Table 1 median exposures against Ueno 2018 Discussion.")

# Published to one decimal; 91.28% prints as 91.2 in the paper (truncated, not
# rounded), so allow a 0.1-point margin beyond the half-unit rounding step.
stopifnot(all(abs(disc$diff_pts) < 0.15))
```

All four rates agree to the printed decimal. The softgel rate without Y93H
computes to 91.28%, which the paper prints as 91.2% (truncated rather than
rounded); the other three round to the published values.

## A flat relationship without Y93H

The Discussion states that, without Y93H, doubling the median exposures of both
drugs raised SVR12 by less than 10 percentage points.

```{r doubling}
p_med <- solve_er(cav_asv_med[["softgel_100"]], cav_dcv_med, 0)
p_dbl <- solve_er(2 * cav_asv_med[["softgel_100"]], 2 * cav_dcv_med, 0)
c(median = 100 * p_med, doubled = 100 * p_dbl, gain_pts = 100 * (p_dbl - p_med))
stopifnot(p_dbl > p_med, 100 * (p_dbl - p_med) < 10)
```

# Replicating Figure 4

Figure 4 of Ueno 2018 shows the predicted SVR12 probability against one drug's
Cav,ss with the other held at its median (ASV 176 ng/mL in the upper panel, DCV
557 ng/mL in the lower panel, per Results), with and without Y93H.

```{r figure4, fig.height = 7}
grid_dcv <- seq(150, 1600, by = 10)
grid_asv <- seq(60, 1000, by = 10)
fig4 <- bind_rows(
  tidyr::crossing(x = grid_dcv, y93h = 0:1) |>
    mutate(panel = "DCV Cav,ss (ASV fixed at 176 ng/mL)", asv = 176, dcv = x),
  tidyr::crossing(x = grid_asv, y93h = 0:1) |>
    mutate(panel = "ASV Cav,ss (DCV fixed at 557 ng/mL)", asv = x, dcv = 557)
) |>
  mutate(
    p = solve_er(asv, dcv, y93h),
    group = ifelse(y93h == 1, "Y93H at baseline", "No Y93H")
  )

ggplot(fig4, aes(x, 100 * p, linetype = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(
    x = "Cav,ss (ng/mL)", y = "Predicted SVR12 (%)", linetype = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the median curves of Figure 4 of Ueno 2018."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r figure4-ends}
fig4_ends <- fig4 |>
  group_by(panel, group) |>
  dplyr::filter(x == min(x) | x == max(x)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  transmute(panel, group, x, p_pct = round(100 * p, 1))
knitr::kable(fig4_ends, caption = "End points of the replicated Figure 4 curves.")
```

The end points match the published curves read by eye: in the upper panel about
81% rising to 99% without Y93H and about 25% rising to 88% with it; in the lower
panel about 90% rising to 98% without Y93H. The lower-panel Y93H curve ends near
79% at 1000 ng/mL, a few points below where the published dotted line ends
(about 82-83%). The published curves are the medians of bootstrap predictions,
not the point-estimate curve, and the Y93H stratum (n = 40) has the widest
bootstrap interval in the figure, so a small offset at the edge of the
exposure range is expected.

# Regenerating the exposures from the PK models

## Virtual cohort

Ueno 2018 derived Cav,ss from the post hoc estimates of the Osawa 2018 PK models.
A virtual cohort is drawn from the demographics in Ueno 2018 Table 1 and passed
through those models. Baseline AST, needed by the asunaprevir model but not
tabulated by Ueno 2018, is drawn from the Osawa 2018 Table 1 distribution
(median 52 U/L, 95th percentile 123.6 U/L), as in the Osawa 2018 article. The
Y93H status is drawn at the observed frequencies.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20180725)
set.seed(20180725)

rlnorm_pct <- function(n, m, p95, lo, hi) {
  pmin(pmax(stats::rlnorm(n, log(m), log(p95 / m) / stats::qnorm(0.95)), lo), hi)
}

arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm, ~n, ~asv_dose, ~softgel,
  "ASV 100 mg BID softgel", 200L, 100, 1L,
  "ASV 200 mg BID tablet", 100L, 200, 0L,
  "ASV 600 mg BID tablet", 50L, 600, 0L
)

cohort <- arms[rep(seq_len(nrow(arms)), arms$n), ] |>
  mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(),
    WT_BASE = rlnorm_pct(dplyr::n(), 55, 75, 36, 93.4),
    CRCL_BASE = rlnorm_pct(dplyr::n(), 84.6, 130, 39.5, 172.8),
    SEXF = stats::rbinom(dplyr::n(), 1, 0.657),
    CONMED_PEGIFN_RBV = 0L,
    AST_BASE = rlnorm_pct(dplyr::n(), 52, 123.6, 13, 595),
    AST = AST_BASE,
    DIS_CIRRHOSIS = stats::rbinom(dplyr::n(), 1, 0.083),
    FORM_ASV_SOFTGEL = softgel,
    y93h_draw = stats::runif(dplyr::n()),
    HCV_NS5A_Y93H = as.integer(y93h_draw < 0.151),
    HCV_NS5A_Y93H_MISSING = as.integer(y93h_draw >= 0.151 & y93h_draw < 0.181)
  ) |>
  select(-y93h_draw, -n)
```

## Steady-state simulation and PKNCA

Each subject is dosed to steady state (`ss = 1`) and observed over one dosing
interval. Cav,ss is the PKNCA average concentration over that interval, with
the `arm` as the grouping variable.

```{r simulate}
# Log-spaced early grid: both PK models carry wide IIV on absorption. The
# grid ends on tau exactly: exp(log(24)) is a hair above 24 in floating point,
# and PKNCA would drop that last sample from the [0, 24] interval.
ss_events <- function(cohort, dose_col, tau) {
  log_grid <- exp(seq(log(0.05), log(tau), length.out = 40))
  obs_times <- c(0, utils::head(log_grid, -1), tau)
  doses <- cohort |>
    transmute(id, time = 0, amt = .data[[dose_col]], evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", ii = tau, ss = 1L)
  obs <- cohort |>
    select(id) |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", ii = 0, ss = 0L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    left_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
    arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

cohort <- cohort |> mutate(dcv_dose = 60)
sim_dcv <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_dcv,
  events = ss_events(cohort, "dcv_dose", 24),
  returnType = "data.frame",
  keep = "arm"
))
sim_asv <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_asv,
  events = ss_events(cohort, "asv_dose", 12),
  returnType = "data.frame",
  keep = "arm"
))
```

```{r pknca}
run_cav <- function(sim, cohort, dose_col, tau) {
  conc <- sim |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
    select(id, arm, time, Cc)
  doses <- cohort |>
    transmute(id, arm, time = 0, dose = .data[[dose_col]])
  intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = tau, cav = TRUE, cmax = TRUE)
  o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | arm + id)
  o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(doses, dose ~ time | arm + id)
  res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals))
  as.data.frame(res$result) |>
    dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "cav") |>
    transmute(id, arm, cav_ngml = 1000 * PPORRES)
}

cav_dcv <- run_cav(sim_dcv, cohort, "dcv_dose", 24)
cav_asv <- run_cav(sim_asv, cohort, "asv_dose", 12)
```

The PKNCA average concentration must equal `Dose / (CL/F * tau)` for each
subject's own clearance. This compares one solve against its own closed form,
so the bound is tight.

```{r mass-balance}
cl_dcv <- sim_dcv |> distinct(id, cl)
cl_asv <- sim_asv |> distinct(id, cl)
mb <- bind_rows(
  cav_dcv |> left_join(cl_dcv, by = "id") |>
    mutate(drug = "daclatasvir", closed = 1000 * 60 / (cl * 24)),
  cav_asv |> left_join(cl_asv, by = "id") |> left_join(select(cohort, id, asv_dose), by = "id") |>
    mutate(drug = "asunaprevir", closed = 1000 * asv_dose / (cl * 12))
) |>
  mutate(rel_err = cav_ngml / closed - 1)
mb |>
  group_by(drug) |>
  summarise(max_abs_rel_err = max(abs(rel_err)), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 5, caption = "PKNCA Cav,ss against Dose / (CL/F x tau).")
stopifnot(all(abs(mb$rel_err) < 0.01))
```

```{r cav-compare}
exposures <- cohort |>
  select(id, arm, HCV_NS5A_Y93H, HCV_NS5A_Y93H_MISSING) |>
  left_join(cav_dcv |> select(id, CAV_DACLATASVIR = cav_ngml), by = "id") |>
  left_join(cav_asv |> select(id, CAV_ASUNAPREVIR = cav_ngml), by = "id")

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug, ~arm, ~published_median,
  "DCV", "All regimens", 557.4,
  "ASV", "ASV 100 mg BID softgel", 163.7,
  "ASV", "ASV 200 mg BID tablet", 268.4,
  "ASV", "ASV 600 mg BID tablet", 590.2
)
sim_medians <- bind_rows(
  exposures |> summarise(sim_median = median(CAV_DACLATASVIR)) |>
    mutate(drug = "DCV", arm = "All regimens"),
  exposures |> group_by(arm) |> summarise(sim_median = median(CAV_ASUNAPREVIR), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(drug = "ASV")
)
cav_tbl <- published |>
  left_join(sim_medians, by = c("drug", "arm")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim_median / published_median - 1))
cav_tbl |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Drug" = drug, "Regimen" = arm,
    "Ueno 2018 Table 1 median (ng/mL)" = published_median,
    "Regenerated median (ng/mL)" = sim_median,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Regenerated Cav,ss medians against Ueno 2018 Table 1.")
```

The regenerated medians are a check on the chain, not a gate: the Table 1
medians are post hoc estimates for the actual patients, whereas the virtual
cohort draws fresh random effects and an AST distribution borrowed from
Osawa 2018. Daclatasvir lands within about 6% of Table 1. Asunaprevir lands
roughly a third above it on the softgel and 200 mg tablet regimens and further
above on the 600 mg tablet. Two documented causes push in that direction. First,
the cohort holds the time-varying AST of the asunaprevir model at its baseline
value, whereas AST falls as the infection is suppressed and a lower AST raises
asunaprevir CL/F (exponent -0.382). Second, the Discussion of Ueno 2018 states
that the popPK model under-predicted exposure in the 600 mg cohort, so the post
hoc Table 1 value for that arm sits below what the typical model predicts. The
exposure-response coefficients were estimated against the post hoc values, so
when the model is fed regenerated exposures the predicted SVR12 is slightly
optimistic. Because the curve is flat without Y93H, the effect on the
predicted rate is small (next section).

## Predicted against observed SVR12

```{r svr-cohort}
exposures <- exposures |>
  mutate(p = solve_er(CAV_ASUNAPREVIR, CAV_DACLATASVIR, HCV_NS5A_Y93H, HCV_NS5A_Y93H_MISSING))

svr_tbl <- exposures |>
  mutate(stratum = case_when(
    HCV_NS5A_Y93H == 1 ~ "Y93H at baseline",
    HCV_NS5A_Y93H_MISSING == 1 ~ "Y93H missing",
    TRUE ~ "No Y93H"
  )) |>
  group_by(stratum) |>
  summarise(n = dplyr::n(), mean_pred_pct = 100 * mean(p), median_pred_pct = 100 * median(p), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(tibble::tibble(stratum = c("No Y93H", "Y93H at baseline"), observed_pct = c(90.3, 47.5)), by = "stratum")
svr_tbl |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Stratum" = stratum, "N" = n,
    "Mean predicted SVR12 (%)" = mean_pred_pct,
    "Median predicted SVR12 (%)" = median_pred_pct,
    "Observed SVR12 (%)" = observed_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Predicted SVR12 in the regenerated cohort against the observed rates (Ueno 2018 Results).")

# Centre-only check, robust to which subjects land in the tails: the median
# prediction in the no-Y93H stratum sits on a flat stretch of the curve.
no_y93h <- svr_tbl$median_pred_pct[svr_tbl$stratum == "No Y93H"]
stopifnot(abs(no_y93h - 90.3) < 5)
```

The median predicted SVR12 in the no-Y93H stratum sits a few points above the
observed 90.3%, consistent with the higher regenerated asunaprevir exposures
described above. The Y93H stratum is small, both in the trial (40 patients) and
in the virtual cohort, and lies on the steep part of the curve, so its
prediction moves with the draw; only the no-Y93H centre is asserted.

```{r svr-plot}
ggplot(exposures, aes(CAV_DACLATASVIR, 100 * p, colour = factor(HCV_NS5A_Y93H, labels = c("No Y93H", "Y93H")))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  labs(
    x = "Regenerated DCV Cav,ss (ng/mL)", y = "Predicted SVR12 (%)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Individual predicted SVR12 in the regenerated cohort."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Placeholder residual error.** The source fits an exact Bernoulli likelihood
  with no random effect and no residual error. rxode2 needs an observation
  declaration, so `prob_svr12` carries a fixed additive SD of 0.001. Sample
  binary outcomes with `rbinom(n, 1, prob_svr12)`.
* **No intercept.** The logit is 0 (probability 0.5) at zero exposure. That
  is an extrapolation far outside the observed range, not an untreated
  response rate.
* **Interaction scaling.** Table 2 prints the interaction as -0.00912 in a row
  headed '(b x 10^-3)'. The packaged value is -9.12e-6, the only reading that
  reproduces the Discussion's model-based rates (see above).
* **Final model only.** The base model (Supplementary Table 2) and the full
  model (Supplementary Table 3) are steps of the covariate search and are not
  packaged; the screened covariates are documented in the model's
  `covariatesDataExcluded`. Supplementary Table 4's refit without the 600 mg
  cohort is a sensitivity analysis and is not packaged either.
* **Printing inconsistencies in the source, none affecting the model.** Table 2's
  bootstrap 95% CI for the interaction (-0.0122 to 0.0154) and for Y93H Missing
  (-2.12 to 705) are not plausible as printed (the interaction's base-model CI
  in Supplementary Table 2 is -0.0122 to -0.00363). The supplement numbers the
  categorical effects differently from the main text (Supplementary Table 3 has
  patient type as CAT1 and Y93H as CAT2; Table 2 has Y93H as CAT1). The
  Results text quotes the softgel median ASV exposure as 164 ng/mL (Table 1:
  163.7) and the Figure 4 fixing value as 176 ng/mL.
* **Missing Y93H coding.** A patient with no baseline result has
  `HCV_NS5A_Y93H = 0` and `HCV_NS5A_Y93H_MISSING = 1`, matching the paper's
  separate missing category against the no-Y93H reference.
* **Regenerated cohort.** Ueno 2018 does not tabulate AST. The baseline AST
  distribution, and the choice to hold time-varying AST at baseline, are taken
  from the Osawa 2018 article. Weight and creatinine-clearance 95th percentiles
  are not printed in Ueno 2018 and were set to plausible values (75 kg and
  130 mL/min) inside the published ranges; peginterferon / ribavirin
  co-medication is 0 because the DUAL regimen does not include it. The
  regenerated exposures use fresh random effects rather than the post hoc
  estimates the authors used, so their medians need not match Table 1 exactly;
  the asunaprevir medians come out about a third higher for the reasons given
  in that section. This affects only the illustrative cohort, not the packaged
  exposure-response model, which takes Cav,ss as data.
* **Figure 4.** The packaged curves are point-estimate predictions. The
  published median curves come from bootstrap replicates, which accounts for a
  few points' offset at the upper end of the Y93H curve in the lower panel.
